evidence.quote: Due to the lack of photometric observations in the UV, the mass-accretion rate could be constrained only indirectly.

referee_caveats_inferred: Dust mass depends on an unstated temperature and on the adopted flux and kappa; no uncertainty is given
The ALMA observation is very short (about 1.3 min per execution) and no image rms or sensitivity is quoted
The eddy stellar mass has a very asymmetric, large error and a fixed inclination from the continuum
Age rests on a single Gaia distance with RUWE 2.6 and on fixed R_V = 3.1; Teff step sizes are coarse
Ring ellipses were traced by eye, so aspect ratios have no formal uncertainties
Binary and planet explanations for the cavity are speculative and not tested with models

missing_for_reproduction: CLEAN mask, threshold, niter, image/cell size and final rms for continuum and 12CO images
Temperature and flux values used for the dust mass
galario/zeus likelihood details and parameter bounds
Exact calibrated execution blocks and the specific self-calibration reference antenna and SNR choices
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Small: two short Band 6 executions from one project; raw data likely a few GB, averaged measurement set much smaller
reproducibility.score_reason: ALMA project code, spectral setup, self-calibration intervals, robust values and key numeric results are given, but imaging masks, eddy and dust-mass settings are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The project code is given and the data should be accessible in the ALMA archive; self-calibration, imaging weights, visibility-fit setup and numeric results (beam, geometry, F_tot, R90) are specified well enough for a partial redo, though dust mass and CO kinematics need unstated choices.

methods_papers.why: JvM correction method followed for the cleaned images
Optical depth relation for the continuum peak
eddy kinematics tool for the stellar mass
IRDAP polarimetric reduction pipeline for SPHERE
Empirical relations for line luminosity to accretion rate
Aspect ratio from ellipse offset and semi-major axis

companion_papers.why: DESTINYS ESO large program under which PDS 111 was observed
Similar temporal variance spectrum approach by the same first author
